notes: Only one included document. Section 2 of the guide repeats the personal-responsibility bullets from section 1; coded once. P66 was used rather than P09 because the guide does not require a syllabus statement. B-only units dropped: the intro phrase 'help you align AI use with your course learning outcomes' (restates the P83 guiding question and describes the templates) and the section 2 restatement of the student-responsibility sentence (exact repeat of the section 1 unit; its fit_note merged there). B's UNCOVERED note on the framework attribution is kept in the fit_note of the P05 unit.

documents.title: UTEP Guidance for Teaching with AI Technologies (Fall 2025: Teaching and Learning in an AI World)
documents.stance_why: The guide says faculty may 'fully embrace AI in your course, allow limited use, or prohibit it altogether' and supplies five sample statements (Free Use, Permitted with Acknowledgement, Brainstorming or Early Stages, Allowed with Permission, Not Permitted). It sets no single university rule and hands the decision to instructors with tiers, so the stance is delegates.
tiers: AI for Brainstorming or Early Stages
documents.summary: Provost guidance leaves the AI decision to each instructor, urging them to explain their rationale and set transparent boundaries. It supplies five sample syllabus statements and a three-level per-assignment framework, and refers misuse to Community Standards under existing integrity policy. A second half offers student-facing best practices on disclosure, verification, ownership and data privacy.

units.resolution_why: Coder A coded modality may, coder B informs. The sentence frames the faculty choice ('fully embrace AI in your course, allow limited use, or prohibit it altogether'); instructors are permitted to choose, so may. Type P04 and actor/phase agreed. B's fuller anchor used.
units.why: The opening says faculty may 'fully embrace AI in your course, allow limited use, or prohibit it altogether', so the decision is left to each instructor. P04 fits because the choice is per course; modality may because it permits instructors to choose.

units.resolution_why: Coder A coded this opening sentence as P66 about the rationale only (course-start); coder B merged rationale, fair boundaries and student ownership into one unit (before-course) with a fit_note. The sentence holds three distinct asks, and the codebook forbids merging rules, so the final splits them: this unit keeps the rationale (P66), the boundaries and ownership asks are separate units. Phase course-start because the rationale is what is communicated to students; B's before-course reading is about design, which the sentence does not stress.
units.why: Faculty are told to 'communicate your rationale clearly' and 'establish fair and transparent boundaries'. This asks instructors to explain the reasons behind their rules, so P66 fits better than P09, which would require a syllabus statement and this does not.
units.anchor: communicate your rationale
units.policy: Instructors communicate their rationale for their AI stance clearly.

units.why: The guidance offers 'ready-to-use syllabus language, guiding questions, and adaptable frameworks', which is the institution supplying templates for instructors (P110).

units.resolution_why: Coder A normalized the policy and put phase before-course; coder B left policy null and put phase general. units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P35, instructor, should, before-course. They differed on unit_stance (A encourage, B neutral). The passage asks instructors to build reflective practice; it does not say anything about whether students may use AI, so neutral. B's fit_note merged with A's.
units.why: Faculty should 'foster student ownership of learning' by 'cultivating reflective and iterative practices'. This asks for reflective assignment design, so P35 (redesign assignments around AI) is the nearest type.

units.policy: Instructors foster student ownership of learning in an AI-enhanced world by cultivating reflective and iterative practices that challenge students to think deeply about their processes.
units.fit_note: Reflective practice is a general pedagogical aim, not a specific redesign.

units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P99 with a weak-fit note, coder B P66. P99 is about easing pressures such as deadlines; this sentence gives the reason for stating expectations ('Clear expectations reduce confusion'), which is the explain-the-rules idea of P66. units.anchor: Clear expectations reduce confusion
units.fit_note: Gives the reason expectations should be clear (they reduce confusion) rather than telling instructors to explain a specific rule. Coder A had judged it a weak fit for P99 because confusion is not a pressure such as a deadline.

units.resolution_why: Coder A normalized the policy, coder B left it null with the anchor 'they must take complete responsibility for its content'. Type, actor, phase and modality agreed. The sentence has two parts (responsibility, and the grade belongs to the student), so A's normalized wording is kept. B also coded the section 2 restatement of this sentence as a separate unit; it is an exact repeat and was dropped, and its fit_note (AI errors become the student's grade) is kept here.

units.fit_note: Stresses that AI errors (logical errors, off-assignment content) become the student's grade.
